checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: One ~10 s vertical video with intelligible English voice-over
must.why: Clip 01 is 10 s vertical, but the speech cannot be checked. The output also holds a 14 s girl clip and a 15 s audio file.

must.item: Narration explains sound reflects off a surface and returns
must.why: The claimed script says this, but it was not transcribed.

must.item: Visuals show sound going from source to surface and back
must.why: Blue rings spread from the shouting kid toward the cliff (frames 2-3). The kid ends with hands at ears, smiling, as if hearing the echo. The return trip is only implied, not clearly drawn.
The script text looks simple, but the audio was not heard, so a cutoff cannot be ruled out.

must.item: Visual journey and spoken explanation agree
must.why: The visuals match the stated script, but the audio is unverified. The extra clips muddy which file is the real deliverable.

faults.what: Extra unrelated 14 s clip of a live-action girl on a black background, ending in black frames, was produced alongside the canyon video. It has nothing to do with echoes. It is not what the user asked for.
Rings do not visibly bounce back from the cliff. The return path is vague and the rings look like swirls.
A separate 15 s audio file is also present, which is not matched to the 10 s video.
The kid's face changes between frames: seen from the side at first, then facing the camera. This is acceptable but slightly inconsistent.

summary: The 10 s canyon cartoon is attractive and shows sound rings going from the kid to the cliff, with the kid reacting at the end. The return bounce is weak, and the stray 14 s girl-on-black clip and 15 s audio file make the deliverable ambiguous.
